title: Highly selective electroreduction of CO2 to C2 products over Cu3N-derived Cu nanowires
abstract: Electrochemical reduction of CO2 to value-added multicarbon products, which can be used as fuels or indirectly as fuel precursors, is a promising approach to reduce CO2 levels and mitigate the energy crisis. However, poor product selectivity is still a major obstacle to the development of CO2 reduction. Here, Cu3Nderived Cu nanowires, with high-density of grain boundaries, are synthesized and demonstrated as an efficient electrocatalyst for electrochemical reduction CO2 to C2 products. The as-prepared catalyst exhibits excellent activity and selectivity for the production of C2 products, with a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 86%, at –1.0 V, and long-term stability during 28 h of electrolysis. The conversion and utilization of CO2 have garnered significant research focus on energy sustainable and eco-friendly future. One should note that the accumulation of CO2 in the atmosphere, which is mainly caused by fossil fuel combustion, raises serious environmental concerns. Electrochemical transformation of CO2 into fuels and other value-added chemicals is considered as an attractive technique to simultaneously achieve carbon recycling and renewable energy storage. Among the wide variety of CO2 reduction products, C2 products are more desirable for a wide range of applications for the chemical and fuels industries due to their high energy density and commercial value than C1 products. For example, as the major C2 products of the copper-based catalysts for electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction, ethylene (C2H4) can be used as a feedstock, e.g., ethylene oxide, polyethylene, and diesel (via ethylene oligomerization), whereas ethanol (EtOH) is also a chemical feedstock (e.g., for ethene, glycol ethers, amines, and esters), a solvent, and a fuel. However, CO2 reduction into fuel is considered as a challenging task due to the multiple protoncoupled electron transfer steps. Thus, the development of catalysts with desirable electronic properties is critically important and industrially required to tune the selectivity of C2 products. To date, significant advances have been made in the development of efficient and robust electrochemical CO2 reduction catalysts. Various techniques, such as nanostructuring, alloying, doping and multi-phasing, are being used to improve the electrochemical performance of CO2 reduction metal catalysts. The creation of intrinsic lattice defects, such as grain boundaries, dislocations and stepped surfaces, is considered as an effective strategy to enhance the performance of CO2 catalysts. The lattice defects serve as additional catalytic sites and tune the electronic and surface properties of nanomaterials. Grain boundaries, as one of the defects, have been used to be served as active sites for improving the electrochemical properties for CO2 reduction into valuable products due to their unique chemical and electronic properties. In particular, computational studies have suggested that the broken local spatial symmetry near the grain boundaries tunes the binding energy of the reaction intermediate facilitating CO2 reduction. Moreover, the experimental studies have been demonstrated that high density of grain boundaries in catalysts is responsible for the active surfaces for enhanced CO2 reduction and the adsorption/desorption of key intermediates at the grain boundaries may be tailored towards the formation of more reduced products like hydrocarbons/oxygenates. For example, Kanan et al. have reported that grain boundaries engendered high activity for CO2 reduction and demonstrated that grain boundary-rich catalysts exhibit the best selectivity. In addition, they have observed a strong correlation between grain boundary surface density and catalytic activity, which suggests that grain boundaries alter the surface properties and lower the barrier for CO2 reduction reaction. Inspired by these studies, we aimed to design and synthesize Cu3N-derived Cu nanowires (NWs). The catalyst with high-density grain boundaries was prepared by electrochemical reduction of Cu3N NWs, where a large negative potential was applied in CO2-saturated 0.1 M KHCO3 aqueous solution. As a result, the Cu3N-derived Cu NWs, with a high density of grain boundaries, were obtained, which exhibited enhanced electrochemical CO2 reduction performance in terms of activity, selectivity and durability. In particular, a maximum Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 86% for C2 products has been obtained, whereas FE of EtOH, C2H6, and C2H4 reached to 8%, 12%, and 66% at –1.0 V (versus reversible hydrogen electrode, RHE), respectively.
